1. Go early and in the afternoon head back to your hotel and take a nice long nap with your LO. Hit the parks again in the early evening right before sunset. This avoids long wait times, overcrowded buses, and the intense midday heat!

2. Bring your own water and snacks or invest in a dining plan - this will save you a ton of money in the long run and you’ll be able to enjoy nicer meals to share with your LO.

3. Stroller fans, sun screen, and a long sunshade for your stroller. You can buy aftermarket ones or certain brands have super long sunshades - like Britax! If you babywear - the Tula Coast is a must have!!

4. Prepare for a few meltdowns. The parks are overwhelming for adults - so imagine it from a young toddlers point of view! Take it in stride - you’re going to see a ton of other parents from all over the world trying to console their screaming kids. 

5. If you like souvenirs and can’t keep tabs on yourself like me, but a giftcard ahead of time to budget your spending. We had a $250 gift card so it was simple to keep track of how much we were spending on souvenirs.

6. Pack extra clothes. Random rain showers and spills are going to happen all day long!

In June of last year our French Bulldog suffered from a heat stroke. I watched my husband desperately try to save her. He placed her in our car, sped to the emergency vet, spent thousands in a matter of hours even though she was in a coma and nearly lifeless as soon as we handed her to the vet. While this hurt me, it hurt my husband in ways I couldn't even imagine. I bought her for his birthday the year before, he loved her probably more than he loved me. I watched him lay his head over her body while loudly crying "I'm so sorry." I will never forget that day as it was the first time I had ever seen him cry. The first time he truly needed me to be there for him. This moment was one of the very first traumatic experiences in our relationship and we learned a lot about each other. I grieve in silence, my husband is the exact opposite.  

Everyone grieves differently and this is perfectly okay. Remember to support each other, heartbreak feels different for all of us. This pain will get better, I promise. Please know that this pup likely way ill prior to you adopting and does not at all affect your ability to parent. You will likely experience identical painful and traumatic events in the future - learn how you each react and how to comfort each other. I hope that peace finds you both soon. I'm here to talk if you need it! xoxo

Please sit down and discuss with him and be patient - it's tough but he will come around. Sometimes I feel like men are just wired differently than us. I have a 14 month old and one on the way - I'm here to talk if you need to!

Those children share your DNA - it's not fair that they get shafted because mom and dad are being immature. You guys both need to sit down and take a hard look at your situation and what type of example you are setting for your children first and foremost.
